ui_bugs.issue: After successful login with /login?next=/rencana user lands on '/' instead of '/rencana'. Root cause: `const nextRaw = new URLSearchParams(window.location.search).get('next') || '/';` is recomputed every render. The submit handler calls navigate(next) with /rencana, but React also runs the useEffect [user,navigate,next]. By the time useEffect fires the URL is already /rencana (no `next=` qs) so nextRaw recomputes to '/', and navigate('/',{replace:true}) overrides. Fix: capture next once via `useState` initializer or `useMemo` keyed on mount (useMemo(()=>…, [])). Also safe to drop the useEffect-based redirect because the submit path already navigates, keeping just a one-shot check when user is pre-authenticated at mount.

Hydration error 'In HTML, <span> cannot be a child of <option>'. Build-time instrumentation wraps the {m} value in a <span>, which React/Chrome reject inside <option>. Rendering still works but logs an error every page load. Workaround: render the numeric minutes outside a JSX expression (e.g. `{`${m} menit`}` as a plain template string or using the array mapper differently) so the toolchain does not inject the span.

React warning: `Received `true` for a non-boolean attribute `target`` — somewhere `target={true}` is being spread onto a native element (probably a span/button). Should be `data-target` or stringified. Non-blocking.

rca of the issue: Login redirect: the next query param is derived from window.location.search inside render. On successful submit the component calls navigate(next); React also schedules a user-change useEffect that will call navigate(next). The submit-driven navigation completes first → URL becomes /rencana (no ?next). The useEffect re-renders Login (still mounted for one tick before Protected unmounts it), nextRaw now resolves to '/' because the search string is empty, and the useEffect calls navigate('/'), overriding the earlier redirect. Fix: freeze next at mount — e.g. `const [next] = useState(() => { const r = new URLSearchParams(window.location.search).get('next') || '/'; return r.startsWith('/') && !r.startsWith('//') ? r : '/'; });`.
